title: Rule-citation content-digest binding: additive schema property + fail-closed loader verification
objective: Add the OPTIONAL content_digest_sha256 property to rule_definition.schema.json citations[] items (64-char lowercase hex, additive - every existing committed rule stays valid) and teach dsl.py::_check_refs to verify, fail-closed at LOAD, that a citation carrying the field matches the resolved snapshot's stored content_digest_sha256 (DSLError naming the rule id and snapshot id on mismatch; absent field loads exactly as before). NO engine change, NO evaluator change, NO new dependency. This is the schema/loader prerequisite the M4-T009 producer report section 4.4 routed to the orchestrator so M4-T009 AS-5 (rules RECORD their citation digest) can be closed without weakening; digest convention is the C3-resolved v1 = sha256(verbatim_excerpt).
business_reason: M4-T009 AS-5 requires every authored rule to RECORD the content digest of the snapshot it was transcribed from, so transcription provenance is bound at the rule file, not only resolved at runtime; the current schema forbids the field (additionalProperties false) and the loader never compares it. Without this unit the R1-R12 FAR family cannot satisfy AS-5 and its gate wave cannot run.
inputs: project-control/tasks/M4-T009.json (AS-5 text - the criterion this unit enables)
project-control/reports/M4-T009-producer-report.md section 4 item 4 (the routed schema/loader scope decision; do not weaken AS-5)
services/api/app/rules/dsl.py (_check_refs - the owning boundary for fail-closed reference validation at load)
services/api/app/_zr_snapshots/v1/zr-23-21.snapshot.json and zr-23-22.snapshot.json (content_digest_sha256 = sha256(verbatim_excerpt), v1 convention per the C3 resolution in docs/MVP_AGENDA.md)

acceptance_scenarios.input: every committed services/api/app/rules/rulesets/*.rule.json validated against the updated schema and loaded via load_rule_file with the default snapshot store
acceptance_scenarios.expected: all existing rules (count asserted, currently 11) validate and load unchanged - none carries the new field yet, and absence is legal; the schema change is purely additive

acceptance_scenarios.input: a CONSTRUCTED rule document (clearly labeled) whose citation carries content_digest_sha256 equal to the cited committed snapshot's stored digest, loaded through build_rule_definition
acceptance_scenarios.expected: loads successfully; the recorded digest is byte-equal to the snapshot's stored content_digest_sha256, which the test independently recomputes as sha256(verbatim_excerpt) - LOADED FROM THE SNAPSHOT, never restated as a literal (M5-T004 tautology lesson)

acceptance_scenarios.input: the same constructed rule with one hex character of the recorded digest flipped
acceptance_scenarios.expected: DSLError raised AT LOAD, message naming the rule id, the snapshot id, and both digests' disagreement class; the rule never becomes evaluable; the assertion matches the mismatch message specifically so a schema-shape rejection cannot satisfy it

acceptance_scenarios.input: constructed citations carrying uppercase hex, 63-char, 65-char, and non-hex values
acceptance_scenarios.expected: each is rejected by schema validation (pattern ^[0-9a-f]{64}$) before any snapshot comparison runs

acceptance_scenarios.input: a constructed rule citing a nonexistent snapshot_id while carrying a digest
acceptance_scenarios.expected: the existing SnapshotError path still raises (resolution precedes digest comparison); the digest check introduces no new resolution path

acceptance_scenarios.input: git diff of the unit; python -m pytest services/api/tests/rules; python tools/modularity_check.py --check
acceptance_scenarios.expected: engine.py and all rulesets untouched; requirements unchanged; full rules suite passes; modularity exit 0

risks: Silent weakening: the mismatch test could pass vacuously against a schema-shape rejection; S3 requires matching the mismatch message specifically.
Back-compat break: a required (rather than optional) property or a wrong pattern would invalidate the 11 committed rules; S1 asserts the full enumeration loads.
path_notes: allowed_paths are EXACT FILES (no globs) deliberately: M4-T009 remains open holding services/api/tests/rules/** and services/api/app/rules/rulesets/**; this packet's only test file is the new test_rule_citation_digest.py, which M4-T009's landed output does not contain, and the two tasks are executed SEQUENTIALLY (M4-T010 produced and gated while M4-T009 awaits its AS-5 unit), so no parallel writer ever shares a file. Exact file paths satisfy both matchers (policy.py path_matches and git_tree_manifest ls-tree) without the dual-form listing.
rulesets/** is FORBIDDEN here on purpose: the family rules adopt the digest inside M4-T009 (its AS-5 unit), keeping each packet's material scope disjoint.

Digest convention is FROZEN by the C3 resolution: content_digest_sha256 = sha256(verbatim_excerpt), already true of every committed v1 snapshot; this unit compares against the snapshot's STORED digest and never recomputes rule-side.
